events.title: The Rule of the Templars approved at Troyes
events.shortBlurb: A council at Troyes gave the young order of the Knights Templar its rule, launching the first of the military orders…
body: On 13 January 1129 a council assembled at Troyes in Champagne under the presidency of the papal legate, Cardinal Matthew of Albano, with bishops and abbots among whom was Bernard of Clairvaux. Before it came Hugh de Payens with five companions, seeking recognition for the brotherhood he had founded at Jerusalem about 1119 to protect pilgrims on the roads of the Holy Land.

The council gave the knights a written rule, the so-called Latin Rule, which Bernard helped to shape. It bound men under the monastic vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience yet sent them to bear arms in defense of Christendom, a union of monk and knight the Church had never before sanctioned.

With this approval the Templars became the first of the great military orders, and Bernard praised the new knighthood in his treatise In Praise of the New Knighthood. Gifts and recruits poured in until the order grew vast in wealth and power; in 1312, under pressure from King Philip IV of France, Pope Clement V suppressed it.
